children: reported fiscal year 2026 revenue of $48.1 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.5 million, while recording a net loss attributable to the company of $11.2 million for the year ended June 30, 2026. Results were driven by a one-time $13.2 million non-cash impairment charge recognized in Q4 and significant production waste from an industry-wide mite issue. The company also completed a rights offering that converted approximately $7.1 million of debt and generated gross proceeds of $12.1 million, enabling repayment of over $19 million of debt obligations.
Revenue: $48.1 million for the year ended June 30, 2026 (FY25: $48.4 million).
Gross profit: $7.9 million, representing 16.4% of sales for FY26 (FY25: $10.1 million, 20.9% of sales).
Operating (loss) profit: Operating loss of $16.9 million for FY26, which includes a one-time non-cash impairment charge of $13.2 million.
Net loss attributable to Bloomia Holdings: $11.2 million for FY26, or a loss of $4.43 per diluted share (FY25: net loss $2.6 million, loss of $1.45 per diluted share).
Adjusted EBITDA: loss of $0.5 million for FY26 (FY25: adjusted EBITDA of $2.0 million).

Production disruption: An industry-wide mite treatment issue in Q4 caused premature bulb aging and resulted in an estimated $2.5 million of excess production waste concentrated in the company's highest-demand quarter.
Input cost pressure: Average tulip bulb costs rose 21% year over year and were further impacted by a 6% unfavorable change in the Euro exchange rate during FY26.

Price actions and mitigation: The company increased selling prices approximately 12% in FY26 and has contracted bulb prices for FY27 near FY25 levels, expecting margin improvement from lower bulb costs.
Operational responses: Management invested in a new mite control treatment for FY27 and continues to pursue automation and operational efficiency initiatives to reduce waste and improve margins.

Capital structure improvement: Completed a rights offering (gross proceeds $12.1 million; ~$5.0 million cash and ~$7.1 million debt conversion), used proceeds to retire over $19 million of debt obligations and reduced total debt to $21.7 million at June 30, 2026 (down from $34.1 million a year earlier).
